\[
q(v) = s \operatorname{round}(v / s),
\quad
s = \frac{255}{L - 1},
\qquad L = 2
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(q(v)\): The nearest level to v
- \(s\): The step between levels
- \(L\): The number of levels
- \(M\): The Bayer matrix, 0 to n^2 - 1

q rounds a value to the nearest of L levels. Error diffusion visits the pixels row by row from the top left, rounds each one, and adds its error e = v - q(v) to neighbors not yet visited. Floyd-Steinberg gives 7/16 of e to the right, 3/16 below left, 5/16 below and 1/16 below right, so all of e is passed on. Atkinson gives 1/8 of e to six neighbors, so only 3/4 of it is passed on. That keeps more contrast and loses detail near black and white. The Bayer method adds s ((M + 0.5) / n^2 - 0.5) before rounding, where M is the Bayer matrix entry at (x mod n, y mod n). Adding 0.5 to M centers the shifts, so their mean is 0.
